A New Documentary Examines the Rise of Cosmetic Penile Procedures

A new feature-length documentary titled *Manhood*, directed by Daniel Lombroso, explores the growing trend of men seeking cosmetic penile enhancement procedures. The film follows various subjects and practitioners, focusing heavily on Bill Moore, an anti-aging aesthetic clinic operator in Dallas who performs a girth-enhancement procedure known as PhalloFill.

According to the documentary, the procedure involves injecting dermal filler to increase girth, though it does not add length. The film highlights how male insecurity has transformed into a lucrative commercial market, capturing the intersection of modern masculinity, social isolation, and the expanding wellness industry.

The Subjects and Practitioners Behind the Trend

*Manhood* introduces several individuals undergoing the procedure, including David, a 24-year-old OnlyFans creator, and Ruben, an out-of-work father of five. Director Daniel Lombroso notes that an overwhelming majority—roughly 75 percent—of the men seeking these treatments at the featured clinic identified as straight, with many leaning conservative.

The film also features commentary from medical professionals. Alex Tatem, a prosthetic urology specialist, points out the psychological limitations of physical modifications, noting that fillers cannot address deeper emotional struggles. Similarly, board-certified urologist Paul Perito raises concerns about non-urologists performing these procedures as the practice expands to dozens of clinics across the United States.

Broader Context and Industry Impact

Data from the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery indicates that men have outpaced women as the fastest-growing demographic for plastic surgery in the US, with nonsurgical cosmetic treatments growing increasingly common among younger generations. The documentary connects these trends to broader cultural phenomena, such as the "looksmaxxing" movement observed in online manosphere communities, where young men pursue extreme physical modifications.

However, the film also documents the financial and personal toll of these treatments. The procedures typically cost between $2,500 and $4,000 per visit, often requiring recurring annual maintenance injections to preserve the desired physical results. For some participants, the mounting costs lead to significant financial strain.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers interested in verifying the details of this report can review the original coverage published by Wired.

  • Confirmed Facts: *Manhood* is directed by Daniel Lombroso and covers aesthetic procedures like PhalloFill offered by practitioner Bill Moore in Dallas. The documentary features multiple subjects, explores the financial costs of recurring treatments, and incorporates insights from medical professionals regarding the commercialization of cosmetic urology.
  • What Remains Unknown: The long-term physical and psychological outcomes for all patients undergoing repeated dermal filler injections in non-traditional clinical settings are not fully detailed in the source text.
